output.brief: The departures are concentrated on one matter, not spread across the group. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel left, against 1 of 13 who never worked on it. Other groups' attrition is flat, so a firm-wide cause such as the hours target, general market movement, or pay across the group doesn't fit. Kestrel associates also recorded far heavier hours (2,270 against 1,940) and worked weekends far more often. The surveys show poor scores on workload and on respect from partners. Every Kestrel associate reports to Dorian Faulk, and he supervises no other matter. So the evidence cannot separate a workload cause from a supervision cause. The exit forms are tick-box and the leavers knew the practice group head might see them, so I give them little weight. Pay as the main driver is unsupported, though a smaller pay effect isn't excluded. A group-wide retention payment would cost £228k, would not address the concentration on Kestrel, and would close the review early, so I advise against it. Next step: run the independent confidential interviews (about £9k, three weeks), with questions that keep supervision and workload apart. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Hold off on moving the supervisor or hiring contract reviewers until the interviews show which cause matters. Confidence is moderate to high on where the problem sits and low on why.
